tagline: Over the lava at McKenzie Pass, and home by Santiam.
intro: Out of Sisters, Route 242 heads west into the Deschutes National Forest on the line of an 1860s wagon road and comes out of the trees onto a lava flow of 65 square miles. At McKenzie Pass, 5,325 feet up, there is lava on every side. West of the summit, Deadhorse Grade drops nearly 1,200 feet in under four miles by hairpin turns.
The loop comes back up the McKenzie River on Route 126, past Sahalie and Koosah falls, then turns east over Santiam Pass and returns to Sisters under the cone of Black Butte, 82 miles around.

moments.title: Dee Wright Observatory
moments.text: An open shelter of lava stone the CCC built in 1935, with windows cut to frame particular peaks and a bronze peak finder on the roof to put names to them.

moments.title: Proxy Falls
moments.text: A 226-foot plunge off a glacier-cut cliff, after which the water sinks into the ground and seems to have no outlet at all. The loop trail is 1.6 easy miles.

moments.title: Clear Lake
moments.text: Snowmelt off Mount Washington spends more than twenty years underground getting here. A hundred feet down stands a forest drowned some 3,000 years ago, still upright in the cold.

practical: McKenzie Pass on Route 242 is closed to motor vehicles by snow from November to July.
